_comment: Trigger-eval query corpus — 7 skills × (10 should + 10 should-not). Should-not queries include at least 3 sister-skill traps per skill (queries that plausibly belong to a sibling and test disambiguation). Each query is a natural user prompt; the eval asks Claude which skill it would invoke (or NONE).
_methodology: Adapted from Anthropic skill-creator's run_loop.py. Vote across K=3 model families (DeepSeek + Nemotron + Mistral) per query for noise-robust scoring. Test set held out 40% per the methodology so iterative description edits don't overfit.

_ambiguity_methodology: Cross-domain prompts that genuinely span 2+ skills. Pass = picked is in {primary} ∪ also_acceptable. Tests robustness when a user's natural-language ask doesn't decompose neatly into one skill — the dominant intent should win, but adjacent skills are also acceptable. NONE is never acceptable here (a skill genuinely applies).

ambiguity_cases.query: lint, test, then audit our deps for CVEs
ambiguity_cases.note: Compound action; lint-and-test is the first verb but dependency-audit is also a valid first call if Claude decomposes
Lint-first phrasing — lint is the gating verb. build-and-release after lint passes is also defensible

ambiguity_cases.query: before I publish, scan the source for hardcoded keys and audit deps
ambiguity_cases.note: Two scan asks; gitleaks (security-scan) is the more specific match for 'hardcoded keys' even though deps audit is also requested

ambiguity_cases.query: is this repo safe to release — check vulns and secrets
ambiguity_cases.note: 'vulns and secrets' splits across the two scan skills; either is a valid first call

ambiguity_cases.query: make sure ruff passes and there's no leaked AWS keys
ambiguity_cases.note: ruff is unambiguous lint; AWS keys is unambiguous gitleaks — Claude must pick one to start

ambiguity_cases.query: ship v2.4.0 — but only if pip-audit comes back clean
ambiguity_cases.note: build-and-release is the goal but conditioned on dependency-audit passing first; either is valid

ambiguity_cases.query: run all the CI checks: lint, test, audit, scan
ambiguity_cases.note: Explicit 4-skill compound — any of the read-only skills is a valid first move; build-and-release is NOT acceptable because it's not a CI check

ambiguity_cases.query: find SQL injection in our handlers and check if our ORM has any CVEs
ambiguity_cases.note: Classic SAST-vs-deps disambiguation but with both intentionally requested. SAST first is the expected dominant verb

ambiguity_cases.query: do a complete pre-release check on the repo
ambiguity_cases.note: Vague 'complete check' — any of the three read-only skills is a defensible first step. build-and-release would be wrong (release is not the action requested)

ambiguity_cases.query: I'm about to npm publish — is everything green
ambiguity_cases.note: 'Everything green' implies CI gates, not the publish itself. Build-and-release is wrong because the user is checking before pushing the publish button
